scenarioStory.history: Unrestrained driver of a sedan that struck a highway median at highway speed and rotated into a guardrail. Prolonged extrication (approximately 12 minutes) due to intrusion on the driver's side. Patient was initially confused, now more responsive but tachypneic and diaphoretic. Right thigh is deformed with an open wound and active bleeding; abdomen is distended and diffusely tender.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew makes contact with the patient just as extrication is completed. He is tachycardic, hypotensive, and pale, with an open right femur fracture actively bleeding and a distended, diffusely tender abdomen suggesting intra-abdominal hemorrhage. → Tourniquet applied, IV fluids started: Crew applies a tourniquet to the bleeding right thigh, establishes large-bore IV access, and begins fluid resuscitation for hypotension. Scene time is minimized in favor of rapid transport given the suspected intra-abdominal hemorrhage. → SBP reassessed, perfusion improving: Following the fluid bolus and hemorrhage control, the patient's blood pressure trends upward toward target. The crew continues serial reassessment en route to the trauma center, anticipating that the abdominal findings may still require surgical intervention.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Multi-system trauma after high-speed motor vehicle crash

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew makes contact with the patient just as extrication is completed. He is tachycardic, hypotensive, and pale, with an open right femur fracture actively bleeding and a distended, diffusely tender abdomen suggesting intra-abdominal hemorrhage.

scenarioEvents.name: Tourniquet applied, IV fluids started
scenarioEvents.description: Crew applies a tourniquet to the bleeding right thigh, establishes large-bore IV access, and begins fluid resuscitation for hypotension. Scene time is minimized in favor of rapid transport given the suspected intra-abdominal hemorrhage.
relatedChecklist: Apply commercial tourniquet 2-3 inches proximal to right thigh wound; mark time
Establish two large-bore IV lines for fluid resuscitation and possible blood products
500 mL crystalloid bolus IV for SBP 82 (below 90 mmHg threshold); reassess after
Minimize scene time (goal under 10 minutes); initiate rapid transport to trauma center

scenarioEvents.name: SBP reassessed, perfusion improving
scenarioEvents.description: Following the fluid bolus and hemorrhage control, the patient's blood pressure trends upward toward target. The crew continues serial reassessment en route to the trauma center, anticipating that the abdominal findings may still require surgical intervention.
relatedChecklist: Reassess SBP after bolus; confirm trend toward 90 mmHg resuscitation target
Transport to highest-level trauma center per field triage guideline

scenarioEvents.name: Tourniquet application delayed
scenarioEvents.description: The crew delays tourniquet application on the actively bleeding right thigh, allowing continued blood loss. The patient's hemodynamic status deteriorates further before hemorrhage control is finally achieved.
relatedChecklist: Immediately apply tourniquet to right thigh; recognize decompensating hemorrhagic shock

scenarioEvents.name: Bolus repeated without reassessment
scenarioEvents.description: The crew repeats fluid boluses without reassessing the patient, missing that the tourniquet is controlling external bleeding but the distended, tender abdomen reflects an internal hemorrhage source that fluids alone cannot fix — only rapid surgical transport can.
relatedChecklist: Reassess SBP and abdomen; recognize non-fluid-responsive shock requires rapid surgical transport
